cases.description: ATX headings and paragraphs; a soft line break stays in the text value as \n.
Emphasis, strong, strikethrough, inline code and a backslash hard break.
A tight bullet list with a nested list indented by the content offset.
An ordered list keeps its start number; markers count up from it.
A blank line between items makes the list spread (loose).
GFM task items: checked is true/false for tasks and null for plain items.
Fenced code with a language, with lang + meta, and with neither.
A blockquote with two paragraphs; ">" alone marks the blank line inside it.
A GFM table with left, right and centre alignment.
Inline links and images, and the three autolink forms written as autolinks.
A thematic break and a raw HTML block.
Setext headings parse as headings and are written in ATX form.
"*" bullets, ")" ordered markers and underscore emphasis are written as "-", "." and "*".
Two adjacent bullet lists: the second is written with the other marker so they do not merge.
A two-space hard break is written as a backslash hard break.
CRLF line endings parse like LF. R preserves them; canonical.md uses LF.
A leading UTF-8 BOM is ignored by the parser, kept by R, and never written by canonical serialization.
Indented code parses as code and is written fenced.
Obsidian's default tab-indented nesting parses as nested; canonical form indents with spaces.
Plain wiki links.
Heading links, block references, aliases, and same-page links with an empty target.
Target and alias are trimmed; an empty alias is null. Canonical form writes the trimmed fields.
Bracket content is raw: escapes are not processed, except that \| is the alias separator.
Code spans, an escaped opening bracket, empty brackets and a line break all prevent a wiki link.
In a table cell the alias separator is written \|; GFM unescapes it before inline parsing.
Standard links to relative .md paths are internal links (kind "markdown"); everything else is external.
Embeds of an attachment with a size hint, of a page section, and inline.
Nested, Unicode and digit-led tags; tags in headings and emphasis; case-insensitive de-duplication in extract.
Headings, mid-word #, digit-only tags, trailing slashes, code and link text.
==text== is a highlight; spaced == is not.
A trailing ^id names the paragraph, including a list item's first paragraph.
A standalone ^id after a table or code block names that block; after a paragraph it stays text.
A folded callout with a formatted title and body; a body-only callout; a title-only callout.
A marker that is not at the start, or has a space after "!", leaves a plain blockquote.
Inline math, prices that are not math (pandoc rule), and a $$ block.
Frontmatter tags (flow sequence, one with a leading #) come first in extract; aliases from a block sequence.
String tags split on commas and whitespace (" #delta" is a YAML comment, so not a tag); a string alias is not split. Canonical form adds the blank line after frontmatter.
Invalid YAML contributes nothing to extract, and the page still parses.
Without a closing line there is no frontmatter: the --- is a thematic break.
A blank line inside an item spreads the item, not the list (mdast's definitions).
Reference links resolve to link/image with the definition's url and title; definitions are not in the tree.
Every row has as many cells as the header: short rows are padded, extra cells dropped.
A line ending inside a code span becomes a space, as CommonMark defines the content.
An HTML block running to the end of the file has no trailing line ending in its value.
GFM footnotes: identifier is the label lowercased, label as written.
Footnote definitions sit at the top level in source order; a definition no reference uses is not in the tree.
A footnote label is letters, digits, - and _. Any other [^…] is plain CommonMark: here a reference link.
ftp:// is an extended autolink (GFM spec 0.29); canonical form writes it in angle brackets.
Inline math never spans a line ending.
$$ blocks are recognised only at the top level; inside a blockquote they are text.
An escaped character never starts an extension: tags, highlights, wiki links, math, block ids, callouts.
Over-escaped input is written with only the escapes the tree needs: the leftmost character of a construct.
A thematic break is *** on the first line of the file and as the first line of a - item; --- elsewhere.
An emphasis directly inside emphasis or strong is written with underscores.
Whitespace that cannot be written literally is a decimal character reference, only where needed.
$x$ when it reads back exactly, otherwise $$x$$.
An info string containing a backtick needs a tilde fence.
An empty blockquote is a lone >.
A bare www. link before punctuation stays bare; the punctuation after it is not escaped.
A heading whose text spans lines is written setext.
A footnote definition writes its first block after the label and indents the rest four spaces.
A destination with a space goes in <...>; a quote in a title is escaped.
Entity references stay undecoded in a bare extended autolink, in both url and text; canonical form writes it bare.
Task items are recognised in any container, blockquotes included.
A task is checked only by its own box, not by [x] later in its text.
A box followed only by its space is an empty task; canonical form keeps that space.
Tasks inside a callout; a first child that is not a paragraph follows a > line in canonical form.
